proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: mewati_akera sūnā “listen!, he heard” (f_h3pigptbpw3zq). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6507.2 *dekṣati gives the dekh- see verb and regional v-/d- variation through transmission. Dekh-ta, dekh-u and ordinary -y past forms retain that stem; dekh-liyo requires the take light verb to be analyzed. Reviewed comparison: Buksa dekʰa “he sees; he saw” (f_uzispb5iudogm). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
